steps.text: Copies DraftKings' public slates and games into the database, refusing any response for another sport.
Captures SIS's counting columns for each team in each game situation, within SIS's two request quotas.
Runs the post-game refresh: games, box scores and play-by-play from CollegeFootballData, and player credit on each play from cfbfastR.
Pulls the week's betting lines from CollegeFootballData.
Reads the current season's rosters from ESPN's team-roster endpoint.
Keeps the week's classic and showdown DraftKings slates and drops any slate already finished.
Joins the slates to their games: every distinct game on the week's slates.
Skips any game already under way.
Reads each game's matchup, roster and fact pack, and refuses to build a game if any of them does not answer.
Runs every recipe over those figures and writes a sentence for each one that clears its volume gate, or a stated absence where it does not.
Writes one comparison table and 14 fixed slots per game, in an order nothing is allowed to re-sort.
Ranks each line's figures within their metric and position on the slate once the whole slate is built, and gives no rank below a minimum field.
Checks every sentence against the banned-phrase list and stops the build before anything is written if one fails.

Marks a figure on the Black Board (the first tab) and player cards (not in this demo) as how often (a tendency), how many (volume), how well adjusted (schedule removed) or how well raw (schedule included).
Filters the week down to this slate's games, in kickoff order.
Adds up the 107 charted defenses into one field figure per slice.
Chooses who gets a block, which with no projection file, as here, is the passer, three backs and five pass catchers by volume.
Divides the vendor's counting columns by its own denominators, so no vendor rate column is ever read.

The gap sweep: for each slice with at least 10 plays, takes the defense's rate, subtracts its own average and the field's lean, and calls a result of 0.5 or more above an opening and 0.5 or more below a wall, the wall only where the offense spends at least 15% of its plays.
Keeps the widest gaps: 5 openings and 4 walls in the pass game, 3 and 2 in the run game, dropping a wide slice when a narrower one inside it already qualifies.
Files a quarterback's own running in the pass-game section, where he is written.
Colors only a figure it judged (a defense's slice against its own average net of the field's lean, an offense's against its own average) and leaves it plain if the same digits could mean two things.
Takes each side's pass-game and run-game rows from the brief.
States who this defense has played and the big games it has allowed, and where no 20-point quarterback, 12-point back or 15-point pass catcher exists, says so and names the highest.
States each chosen player's own figures in the slices his position is read in and in the slices the sweep found.
Lays out each game's market and pace table.
Marks every player, team, percentage and rank in a line, each drawn one way throughout.
In the real tool a model then words the fact pack, with a verdict or bet refused and a figure the pack did not carry flagged, and those paragraphs are off in this demo.

outputs.feeds: Player pool: every game read top down, from how it is likely to go to each unit and its players, with their salaries.
Player pool: which games on the slate carry the most scoring and pace, before any player is looked at.
Player pool: whether a team's pass catchers or its backs have the stronger way into this defense.
Player pool: which positions have already scored against this defense, and against whom.
Player pool: which offense has a real opening, and which of its players sit on it.
Exposure: where a popular player runs into a wall his offense leans on.
Player pool: one player's figures in the same slices as the defense's.
Player pool: which games and sides merit a closer look, from one side-by-side view of both teams.
Exposure: how the game may flow and who holds the volume.
Exposure: single stated figures about a team or player, each with its sample.

legend.head: three kinds of number, three looks, each with its own spectrum · the same everywhere on the site

rows.name: HOW OFTEN
rows.text: a share or a tendency. Blue, deeper the more unusual. Never good or bad.

rows.name: HOW MANY
rows.text: volume: plays, dropbacks, carries, targets. Grey. Set by game state.

rows.name: HOW WELL · ADJUSTED
rows.text: quality with the schedule removed. Bright ramp. Read first.

rows.name: HOW WELL · RAW
rows.text: quality as it happened, schedule included. Same ramp, muted, dotted edge, with its games. Weigh it by the games and who they were against.

legend.note: A rank always carries its word: 0–24 WEAK · 25–39 BELOW · 40–59 AVERAGE · 60–74 ABOVE · 75–100 STRONG. A count under the floor prints yellow and takes no color. When a raw figure and its adjusted figure sit in different bands, the row says so.
